Found under Settings, Tools, Email aliases.

<a id="page-aliases"></a>

## About this page

Makes email addresses to give to sites instead of your real one. You can see which site passed an address on, and with a forwarding service, stop its mail without touching your inbox.

#### How it works

The first group works from the address you already have. It needs no service and no network.

The second group uses a forwarding service you have an account with. Each alias it makes is a new address that forwards to your real one, and you can switch any of them off.

#### When to use it

A plus tag is enough to see which site leaked or sold your address. A forwarding service is for when a site should never learn your real address at all.

See also [With your own address](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-own), [Forwarding services](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-services), [Use an alias](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-use-alias), [Aliases and forwarding](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-aliases).

<a id="group-aliases-own"></a>

## With your own address

Two ways to make your own address look different to each site. Mail sent to either still lands in your inbox.

#### How it works

A plus tag puts a word after your name: you+shop@gmail.com. Gmail, Fastmail and many other mail services deliver it to you.

Gmail ignores dots in the name, so firstlast@gmail.com and first.la.st@gmail.com reach the same inbox.

Both are worked out on this device. Nothing is sent anywhere, and they work with network features off.

#### Limits

Neither hides your real address. It is there to read in both, and a site that strips the tag or the dots has it as it is.

See also [Plus tag](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-alias-plus), [Gmail dots](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-alias-dots), [Forwarding services](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-services).

<a id="action-alias-plus"></a>

## Plus tag

Adds the tag to your address after a "+", such as you+github@gmail.com.

#### How it works

The tag becomes lowercase letters, digits and dashes, and needs at least one letter or digit. A tag already in the address is replaced.

Copy the result with the button beside it.

#### Limits

A site can remove the tag before it stores the address, and then it has your real one.

See also [With your own address](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-own), [Gmail dots](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-alias-dots).

<a id="action-alias-dots"></a>

## Gmail dots

Puts dots at random places in a Gmail address. Gmail ignores them, so the mail still reaches you.

#### How it works

Each click places the dots differently. Only gmail.com and googlemail.com addresses are accepted, because other services treat a dot as part of the name.

#### Limits

A site that removes the dots has your real address.

See also [With your own address](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-own), [Plus tag](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-alias-plus).

<a id="group-aliases-services"></a>

## Forwarding services

Makes a new address at a service you have an account with. Mail to it is forwarded to your real inbox until you switch it off.

#### Why it is there

The site never sees your real address. If it leaks or sells the alias, you switch that one alias off and nothing else changes.

#### How it works

Choose the service, paste the API key from your account there, and click **Keep this key in the vault**. From then on the page can make aliases and list the ones you have.

The key is saved as an API key item in your vault, named after the service, such as "SimpleLogin API key". For each call, WM Pass reads it from the vault and wipes its copy straight after.

With a key kept, opening the page or choosing the service asks it for your aliases. DuckDuckGo is the exception: it cannot list them.

The service you choose receives your API key with every call, and the note you write when you make an alias. Each service says exactly where its calls go.

#### Limits

Every mail to your aliases passes through the service, so it can read them. Choose one you trust with your mail.

WM Pass finds the key by its item's name. Rename or delete that item and the page asks for a key again.

Needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

See also [SimpleLogin](/guide/settings/aliases/#concept-alias-simplelogin), [addy.io](/guide/settings/aliases/#concept-alias-addy), [Firefox Relay](/guide/settings/aliases/#concept-alias-firefox-relay), [DuckDuckGo](/guide/settings/aliases/#concept-alias-duckduckgo), [Keep this key in the vault](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-alias-keep-key), [Aliases and forwarding](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-aliases).

<a id="concept-alias-simplelogin"></a>

## SimpleLogin

Makes aliases at SimpleLogin with an API key you create under API Keys in your SimpleLogin account.

#### How it works

Every call goes to app.simplelogin.io with your API key. Making an alias also sends the note you wrote, which SimpleLogin saves with it.

Each new alias is made of random words. Your aliases are listed on the page, and each one can be switched off.

See also [Forwarding services](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-services), [Forwarding on](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-alias-forwarding).

<a id="concept-alias-addy"></a>

## addy.io

Makes aliases at addy.io with an API key you create in addy.io's settings.

#### How it works

Every call goes to app.addy.io with your API key. Making an alias also sends your note, which addy.io saves as the alias's description.

Each new alias is made of random words on the anonaddy.me domain. The page lists up to 100 of your aliases, and each one can be switched off.

See also [Forwarding services](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-services), [Forwarding on](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-alias-forwarding).

<a id="concept-alias-firefox-relay"></a>

## Firefox Relay

Makes Relay addresses with the API key from your Firefox Relay settings.

#### How it works

Every call goes to relay.firefox.com with your API key. Making an address also sends your note, which Relay saves as its description and as the site it was made for.

Your Relay addresses are listed on the page, and each one can be switched off.

See also [Forwarding services](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-services), [Forwarding on](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-alias-forwarding).

<a id="concept-alias-duckduckgo"></a>

## DuckDuckGo

Makes a Duck address with the token from your DuckDuckGo Email Protection dashboard. It is experimental.

#### How it works

DuckDuckGo has no public API, so this uses the private one its own extension calls, at quack.duckduckgo.com. Only the token is sent: your note stays on this device. The new address ends in @duck.com.

#### Limits

It may stop working whenever DuckDuckGo changes that private API.

Duck addresses cannot be listed or switched off here. Manage them from DuckDuckGo.

See also [Forwarding services](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-services).

<a id="action-alias-keep-key"></a>

## Keep this key in the vault

Saves the service's API key as an item in your vault, so the page can use it.

#### How it works

The item is an API key named after the service, such as "addy.io API key". It is encrypted, synced and backed up with the rest of the vault, and you can open it from the vault list like any other item.

#### Limits

Anyone with this key can make aliases in your account and switch them off. If you think it has leaked, revoke it at the service and keep a new one here.

See also [Forwarding services](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-services).

<a id="action-alias-make"></a>

## Make a new alias

Asks the service for a new alias, with what you typed under "What is it for?" as its note, and copies the new address.

#### How it works

The address goes on the clipboard, and into the list on the page for services that can list them. A note such as the site's name helps you tell your aliases apart later.

See also [Forwarding services](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-services), [Use an alias](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-use-alias).

<a id="action-alias-forwarding"></a>

## Forwarding on

The switch beside each alias. Off stops its mail reaching you; on starts it again.

#### How it works

The list reloads after each change, so it always shows what the service says.

#### Limits

SimpleLogin only offers a switch that flips the alias. If it was changed somewhere else since the page loaded, it can end up the other way: check the list after it reloads.

See also [Forwarding services](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-services).

<a id="action-use-alias"></a>

## Use an alias

The button beside a login's username in the editor. It makes a new alias at a service you have set up and puts it in the field.

#### How it works

Every service with a key kept in the vault is offered. The item's name is sent as the alias's note, so you can tell later which site it is for.

With no service set up yet, it offers **Set one up**, which opens Settings, Tools, Email aliases.

#### When to use it

When you sign up somewhere new and want the site never to have your real address.

#### Limits

Needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

See also [Forwarding services](/guide/settings/aliases/#group-aliases-services), [Make a new alias](/guide/settings/aliases/#action-alias-make).
